title: Al-Khabir, the All-Aware
hookLine: the All-Aware, of every inner detail
tomorrow: a stranger does something shocking in the mosque. then what?

cards: Fourth try on the photo. The good angle, the light fixed, the caption rewritten until it sounds effortless. You can fool a feed.

The harder question, yesterday's, is whether you can fool yourself. A head can run its own highlight reel too: the version where we were right, where it wasn't our fault. Today's Name doesn't see the reel.

teach.b: Al-Khabir, the All-Aware, who knows every inner detail: not just what happened, but the why under it. The Qur'an asks, in Pickthall's words: "Should He not know what He created? And He is the Subtile, the Aware."
Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight.
The Aware sits right next to the Subtle, yesterday's Name, in that verse. Whoever knows you down to the last detail is also the one who is gentle. Being known that well is not a trap.
That's why honesty with yourself isn't a confession to someone who'll be shocked. He already knows.
Now walk back through the week. The one who humbles: status passes. The one who hears: a whisper reached Him.
The one who sees: a warning and a comfort. The Judge: the last word on a person isn't ours. The Just: fair, even against yourself.
The Subtle: kindness you see looking back.
And today, the Aware, who holds all of it, including the parts you'd rather crop out.

how: Muslims practice muhasabah, taking honest account of oneself, often at night before sleep, trusting that Allah, al-Khabir, already knows what is inside.

o: the All-Aware, of every inner detail
the one who records news for the last day
the one who knows only what we say aloud

games.q: this week's Names — tap the pairs.
p: the last word on a person

s: being honest with yourself means beating yourself up
the Aware is named beside the Subtle and Kind. known, and not shamed.
in 67:14, the All-Aware sits right beside the Subtle
"And He is the Subtile, the Aware."

games.q: after a fight with your mom, you replay it in your head, and you're the hero every time. what fits Al-Khabir?
o: keep replaying it until you feel fully in the right.
ask what part was yours; He already knows the whole of it.
decide it was all your fault so you can stop thinking.
games.why: the Aware sees the raw footage, not the reel. honesty means finding your part, neither all of it nor none of it.

practice: Close your eyes and ask yourself one honest question you've been stepping around this week: what part of this is mine? Don't argue with the answer or explain it away.
Let it come, and let it sit beside you for the two minutes, known and not shamed.

wordCard.voice: Al-Khabir. The All-Aware, of every inner detail, named right beside the Subtle and Kind.

carryVoice: Carry this: aware of everything, the reel and the raw footage, and gentle with both. That's a week of Names.
